rfcs.title: RSA/SHA-1 SIGs and RSA KEYs in the Domain Name System (DNS)
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc3110_rsasha1_algorithm is queryable because all fields it references exist in the OpenINTEL dictionary: algorithm (integer).
rfcs.note: Algorithm 5 is deprecated for signing by RFC 9905 (Nov 2025). A match here is historical deployment; RFC 9905 reads it as non-conformance.

rfcs.title: DNS Security Introduction and Requirements (DNSSEC base: RFC 4033/4034/4035)
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc4033_base_dnssec_record_present is queryable because all fields it references exist in the OpenINTEL dictionary: rr_type (string).
rfcs.note: Modelled as one combined entry because the three documents are published together and are not separable from record-level observations alone. A match here should be read as 'base DNSSEC deployed', not as adoption of a specific mechanism.

rfcs.title: Resource Records for the DNS Security Extensions
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc4034_core_record_present is queryable because all fields it references exist in the OpenINTEL dictionary: rr_type (string).
rfcs.note: Matched on format details rather than record presence, so that it says something RFC 4033's broad 'any DNSSEC record' indicator does not.

rfcs.title: Protocol Modifications for the DNS Security Extensions
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc4035_dnssec_ok_negotiated is non-queryable because none of the fields it references exist in the OpenINTEL dictionary: dnssec_ok_flag. No part of it can ever be evaluated against the measurement corpus.
rfcs.note: Expected to classify as non-queryable against a zone-file corpus. That is the correct answer, not a gap: OpenINTEL forward DNS records what zones publish, not how resolvers and servers negotiate.

rfcs.title: Use of SHA-256 in DNSSEC Delegation Signer (DS) Resource Records
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc4509_ds_sha256_digest is queryable because all fields it references exist in the OpenINTEL dictionary: rr_type (string), digest_type (integer).
rfcs.note: Digest type 2 is now the de-facto default, so a match indicates the mechanism is in use rather than that the operator made a deliberate recent choice.

rfcs.title: DNSSEC Operational Practices, Version 2
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc6781_ksk_zsk_separation is ambiguous: every field it references exists in the OpenINTEL dictionary (rr_type (string), flags (string)), so it can be evaluated, but the checklist marks it ambiguous because the same observation is equally well explained by other RFCs, so a match is not uniquely attributable to RFC 6781.
rfcs.note: Recommendations, not wire format. The KSK/ZSK split is weakly visible via the DNSKEY SEP bit but is not evidence this document was followed.

rfcs.title: Clarifications and Implementation Notes for DNS Security (DNSSEC)
rfcs.reason: Indicator rfc6840_mandatory_algorithm_rules is non-queryable because none of the fields it references exist in the OpenINTEL dictionary: name_algorithm_set_consistency. No part of it can ever be evaluated against the measurement corpus.
rfcs.note: Not measurable *here*, for a specific and fixable reason. Its section 5.11 mandatory-algorithm rules are genuinely visible in published zone data, but they are set comparisons across the DS, DNSKEY and RRSIG records at one name, and this pipeline's indicators are per-record predicates. An earlier version of this entry matched 'any DNSSEC record', which is the evidence RFC 4033 already claims; it attributed 1.8 million observations and a first-seen date to a document whose actual requirements were never tested.

rfcs.note: RFC 8078 builds directly on these record types, so a CDS/CDNSKEY delete signal matches both RFCs; RFC 8078 must rank higher because it adds a further, more specific condition.
